text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- The nationalist LNNK party held its 10th congress on Saturday where most delegates favoured a merger with the Fatherland and Freedom party, which has more seats in parliament.
- Speaking at a meeting of the intra-parliament body the Baltic Assembly in Parnu, Prime Minister Andris Shkele called for the creation of a Baltic customs union.
- Latvia's hockey team lost 4:5 to the U.S. at the World championship.
- Shkele rejects Lattelekom's demands for compensation if the government cuts short the telephone company's monopoly.
DIENA
- The text of a border treaty between Latvia and Russia was given final approval by delegations of the two countries meeting in Moscow last Friday.
- The Baltic Assembly passed a resolution which calls on NATO to start admission talks with at least one of the Baltic states.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- The prime ministers of Latvia and Estonia agreed on establishing a common border check point.
- Shkele said he would not attend protest actions planned by Latvian farmers for Wednesday.
- In 1993-1996, 338 people lost their lives at work.
BIZNES & BALTIJA
- Shkele said he would cut the number of his bodyguards from 5 to 1.
- Only 2,500 of Latvia's 50,000 companies have submitted their 1996 accounts, which were due on May 1.
DIENAS BIZNESS
- The chairman of the Latvian Association of Transit Business, Aivars Lembergs, blames EU PHARE for incorrect forecasts which are hampering the development of the Latvian ports sector.
- Last month saw an improvement in major macroeconomic indicators in Latvia, the ministry of economics said.
